title: A 0.4µW/MHz Reference-Replication-Based RC Oscillator with Path-Delay and Comparator-Offset Cancellation Achieving 9.83ppm/°C from -40 to 125°C
problem: Open-loop RC oscillators struggle with frequency stability against process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) variations due to path-delay and comparator offset sensitivity; closed-loop approaches achieve better stability but incur significant area, power, and circuit complexity overhead.
motivation: RC oscillators are critical timers in IoT and edge devices; improving free-running frequency stability without complex compensation networks or switched-resistor calibration is essential for ultra-low-power operation.
method: The circuit uses an internal reference copy to detect and cancel two major sources of frequency drift: signal propagation delay (time for signals to travel through the circuit) and comparator offset (built-in errors in the voltage-comparison stage). Correction circuits integrated into the design automatically compensate for these effects without needing adjustable resistors or complex mathematical calibration. This achieves ±9.83ppm/°C frequency stability (less than 10 parts per million drift per degree Celsius) across -40°C to 125°C while using only 0.4µW/MHz of power.
key_novelty: An open-loop oscillator that internally cancels propagation delay and comparator errors, matching the stability of closed-loop designs while avoiding their circuit complexity.
contributions: Path-delay and comparator-offset cancellation for improved stability
9.83ppm/°C temperature coefficient across wide temperature range
primary_theme: Stable low-power RC oscillator for IoT timing
